item.description:
Lectern 1.2.0

Flashcards saved in pages, Summarise Subject with PDF export, and clearer Ollama setup

Added

  • **Summarise Subject…** in a subject's ⋯ menu (under Glossary): reads every page in the subject and writes a brief summary of the important content (overview, topic by topic, key terms, how ideas connect, focus for the exam) to a “📋 Subject Summary” page you can edit. Large subjects are summarised in parts, so it works with local Ollama models too.
  • **Export Summary as PDF…** in the subject's ⋯ menu (under Archive Subject): exports the finished summary as a PDF with a cover page.
  • Flashcards you make from a page are also saved in that page, in a “🃏 Flashcards” section: each card is a toggle (click the question to see the answer), with a link to the deck where they're studied. This covers AI-generated cards, “Make flashcard” from highlighted text and New Flashcard from a page.
  • An “Open Ollama” button in Settings → AI and on AI errors when Ollama isn't running on your Mac.

Fixed

  • When the chosen Ollama server (for example ollama.com) doesn't have the selected model, Settings → AI now says so and offers “Use Local (this Mac)”, and the error names the server instead of saying the model is missing.

Lectern 1.1.0

Ollama support, sidebar ⋯ menus, notes from a link, and a formatting toolbar with comments

Added

  • Ollama as an AI provider (Settings → AI), like Atlas's Local mode: use free models running on your Mac (localhost:11434), or Ollama's hosted models at ollama.com with an Ollama API key kept in the Keychain. Every AI feature works with it; models that can see images also explain diagram slides. Onboarding offers “Use Ollama instead”.
  • A ⋯ button on subjects and folders in the sidebar (and on pages when you point at them) with New Page, New Folder, Rename, Duplicate, Move, Show in Finder, Export and Move to Trash, so you don't need to right-click.
  • “Notes from a link” on every page: paste a link to an article, PDF, PowerPoint, Word file or Google Doc (or open one in Lectern's browser if it needs your iLearn login), and the AI adds a summary, key points, notes, key terms and questions to the bottom of the page. The link is saved in the page's sources.
  • A formatting toolbar above every page: text style (Text, Title, Heading 1–3, Quote, Code), font size, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, text colour, highlight colour, links, comments, lists and undo/redo. Underline and Comment are also in the selection toolbar.
  • Comments: select text and add a note to it; click the text to read, edit or resolve the comment. Comments, colours and sizes are saved in the Markdown, so they survive opening the page elsewhere.
  • Settings → Appearance can hide the formatting toolbar.

Fixed

  • Lectern now always opens its main window when it starts, even if the window was closed when you last quit.

Lectern 1.0.0

First release

Added

  • A University folder you choose (iCloud Drive or OneDrive for automatic backup): every subject, folder and page is a normal file. Pages are Markdown with YAML front matter; attachments, flashcards and quizzes sit beside them.
  • Subjects with unit code, name, semester, convenor, colour, emoji, credit points and assessments, plus starter folders (Lectures, Practicals & Tutorials, Readings, Assessments, My Notes, Exam Prep, Flashcards). Semesters group subjects; archive a subject at the end of semester.
  • A sidebar tree with drag and drop, right-click menus (new page or folder, rename, duplicate, move, show in Finder, export, move to Trash) and remembered folders. Deleted items go to the macOS Trash.
  • Page templates: Lecture, Practical/Tutorial, Reading, Assessment (countdown, weight, status, checklist progress), Note and Exam Prep (topic confidence ratings). Every page shows its breadcrumb, tags, last-edited time and backlinks.
  • A block editor that saves to Markdown: “/” menu (headings, lists, checklists, quotes, callouts, toggles, tables, code with highlighting, KaTeX maths, dividers, images, embedded PDFs, page links), Markdown shortcuts, pasted and dropped images, [[page links]] with autocomplete that survive renames, a floating toolbar with highlight colours and AI actions (Explain, Make flashcard, Simplify), word count, focus mode and typewriter mode.
  • Lecture slides → notes with Claude: paste a PDF, PowerPoint, Word, web page, Google Slides/Drive link, or drop files; sign in to iLearn once in Lectern's own browser; bulk-import a folder of slides (one page per file, numbered by week). Text, speaker notes and diagram images are extracted; long decks are written in parts then merged. Notes include an overview, objectives, topic notes with clickable slide citations, diagrams explained, key terms (added to the subject glossary), a summary, likely exam questions and things to clarify. A cost estimate is shown first, and every step can be cancelled.
  • On-device transcription of lecture recordings (Apple Speech), used together with the slides.
  • The slide viewer beside the notes: click a slide to see the notes that came from it.
  • Flashcards with FSRS-6 spaced repetition: basic, reversible, cloze and image occlusion cards; fast entry; cards from highlighted text or generated from notes; due, cram and weak-card modes; keyboard grading; daily reminder; stats (heatmap, retention, forecast); CSV import/export and Anki export.
  • Quizzes and timed practice exams from a page, folder or subject, with AI marking of written answers, weak topics and “make flashcards from my mistakes”.
  • Study Coach per subject (advice from assessments, flashcards, quizzes, confidence ratings and study time; evidence-based techniques; “Plan my week”) and “Ask about this subject”, answered from your own notes with clickable sources.
  • Home dashboard, week/month planner with drag-to-reschedule, optional Apple Calendar sync, a Pomodoro study timer in the menu bar, and a grade calculator with Australian grade bands.
  • Global search (pages, slide text, transcripts and flashcards), command palette (⌘K), recent and pinned pages, back/forward, subject glossary.
  • Export a page, folder or subject as PDF (with a cover page), Markdown or HTML; print; a subject study guide PDF; copy as Markdown; one-click full backup zip.
  • Version history (the last 50 versions of each page) with preview and restore.
  • Onboarding, a Demo Subject (Intro to Psychology), Sparkle updates, and a Privacy tab that explains exactly what is sent to Anthropic and when.
